the MHV vertices in gauge theory are obtained by a simple prescription, the parity transformation, the charge conjugation, and the dual Ward identities are discussed, and the MHV vertices with fermions are obtained.
the MHV vertices are the most efficient way to calculate scattering amplitudes and the Cachazo, Svrcek and Witten approach is an efficient way to calculate MHV vertices.
the generic MHV amplitudes in QCD are computed by using a new approach to perturbatively calculate in QCD and the results are consistent with the previously well known results.

the computation of the generic amplitudes in the N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory.
the computation of tree-level scattering amplitudes of massless gluons and fermions.
the study of the scattering amplitudes of massless particles in the framework of gauge theory and gravity.

the MHV vertices and the corresponding MHV amplitudes in the gauge theories are well understood.

the Cachazo et al. approach to perturbatively computing scattering amplitudes has been generalized to include fermionic fields and the results are correct.
